description: Fleet session-management Phase B, D1 (AMEND 5b), with EFFECT VERIFICATION added 2026-08-18 (GAU-09). Sends '/clear' over the resolved host driver's driver channel to the running agent process behind agent_instance_id, then -- where that driver can read its target back -- polls for a positive cleared-state signature before answering. Optional park=true additionally drives the ledger row from live/idle/overdue to parked (L3 rule 2, steward direction), the ONLY writer of that lifecycle edge; park is skipped when a verification was attempted and failed, so an unproven clear never leaves a park behind in the ledger. Only available on hosts whose driver provides a driver channel (currently 'headless' and 'tmux'); the degenerate 'operator' driver, and a headless/tmux process this build's memory no longer tracks (e.g. after a restart), both refuse with unsupported_on_host rather than silently doing nothing.
embedding_description: Nuke a fleet session's memory back to zero via '/clear' -- every prior turn gone, unrecoverable, with an optional park flag to retire the ledger row too. The panic-button verb, for corrupted context or a hard reset. Reports whether the clear was actually OBSERVED, not merely sent. Nothing here reduces size gently -- that is compact_session. terminate_session ends the process, not just its memory.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: lifecycle_state (the row's state after this call); parked (true only when park=true was passed and the live/idle/overdue -> parked transition actually landed); dispatched (the '/clear' reached the driver channel); cleared (true only on a POSITIVE observation that the target is now clear, null when this driver has no read-back surface -- never false, because a driver that looked and saw nothing raises clear_unverified instead); and clear_verification, naming which of those produced it: 'confirmed' or 'unsupported_on_driver'.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Read 'cleared', not success. A successful call means the command was DISPATCHED; only cleared=true means the clear was observed to take effect. When cleared is null, say plainly that this driver cannot confirm the effect and the clear is unverified -- never round that up to 'cleared' or report it as done. This verb previously returned a success shape for a clear that never happened, so do not reintroduce that reading in prose.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Reads the managed_session ledger row, refuses on a terminal lifecycle_state, resolves the row's host driver, sends '/clear' over its driver_channel(), then verifies the effect on drivers implementing the ClearVerifyingDriverChannel protocol (the tmux channel reads its pane with capture-pane; the headless stream-json channel has no pane and reports unsupported_on_driver). A fixed sequence with NO retry loop anywhere in it.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: session_not_found: no managed_session row exists for the given agent_instance_id. lifecycle_state_conflict: the row is already terminated/retired -- terminal rows never receive driver-channel commands. unsupported_on_host: the row's host has no driver in this build, or its driver has no live driver channel for this host_ref (the degenerate 'operator' driver, or a headless process spawned before a restart wiped this build's in-memory tracking). driver_delivery_failed: the channel itself rejected the send. clear_unverified: the '/clear' WAS dispatched but the driver read the target back and never observed a cleared state -- the send happened, the effect did not.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For clear_unverified, DO NOT re-send: the '/clear' text is already sitting in that session's input buffer, and a blind retry deposits a second copy while still being unable to confirm itself. The usual cause is that the target was mid-turn, so the injected text was taken as an ordinary message rather than a command; clear it externally instead (for a tmux-hosted pane, send the text and the Enter as SEPARATE bursts). A session cannot clear ITSELF through this verb by construction -- the caller is mid-turn precisely because it is the thing making the call. For unsupported_on_host, use the manual equivalent for that session -- this verb has no fallback path, by design, to avoid a silent no-op.
